newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kesko says sells Tuko for FIM 2.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Kesko says sells Tuko for FIM 2.2 bln.

text.p: Finnish wholesale and retail group Kesko Oy said on Friday it had agreed to sell its Tuko daily goods operations to various Finnish buyers for 2.2 billion markka.
"The total value of the deal is 2,156 million markka," Kesko said in a statement.
Kesko said it did not sell the daily goods operations belonging to the Anttila department store chain and that the transactions would not have any significant impact on Kesko's financial position.
Kesko sold the TukoSpar Oy logistics and purchasing unit to Heinon Tukku Oy, Sentra Oy, Oy Stockmann Ab and Wihuri Oy, it said.
It sold Tuko's Suomen Spar Oy unit -- excluding the Metro wholesales and cash-and-carry operations which Wihuri Oy bought -- to Sentra Oy.
Kesko also said its Tuko unit would acquire Sentra's Carrols fast food chain for 90 million markka.
Tuko's real estate relating to the disposed operations was sold to a real estate company owned by pension insurers Elake-Varma, Elake-Sampo, life insurer Nova and insurance group Sampo.

Stockmann said in a separate statement that the total price for Tukospar was 235 million markka, of which its portion was 32.9 million and Sentra said in a statement that it paid 253 million markka for Suomen Spar.
Stockmann said its share of Tukospar would be 14 percent, while Wihuri would own 44 percent, Sentra 35 percent and Heinon Tukku seven percent.
The operations involved had 1996 net sales of 7.3 billion markka, Kesko said, adding the transaction would come into force if the European Commission approved it by April 30.

Kesko last May said it planned to merge with its rival Tuko, but the European Commission blocked the transaction in November on the basis that it would damage competition on the Finnish daily goods market.
